title: No. 6
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shion, a privileged student in the seemingly perfect city-state No. 6, shelters a fugitive boy called Nezumi (Rat) during a typhoon and loses his elite status. Years later he uncovers a government cover-up involving parasitic wasps, is rescued by Nezumi and lives in the slums of West Block, where their bond deepens into romance as they confront the city's secrets. A manga adaptation of Atsuko Asano's novels.
life_message: Compassion and truth are worth more than comfort under an unjust order, and love can cross every wall.

Order vs freedom.evidence: A controlled utopia is the villain; freedom outside the wall.

folkways.japan: Shion's polite, sheltered upbringing versus Nezumi's outsider bluntness plays on Japanese inside-outside (uchi-soto) distinctions.

delivery.evidence: ANN's final-volume review notes long stretches explaining the truth about the city, dense but rarely info-dumping; officials shown as cruel.

personified.ideology: control and order over human life

delivery.note: Its critique of the controlled city is carried by the plot and, in the last volume, by lengthy explanation of the city's secrets.

winners_losers: Shion and Nezumi expose the city's lie; the controlling regime loses. Sympathy goes to the outcasts and their love.
to_verify: Delivery rests on one critic: Rebecca Silverman (ANN review of the final manga volume); earlier volumes not checked
